name: Luis Munoz Marin International Airport
before:
Puerto Rico's main airport and the busiest in the insular Caribbean, handling 13,643,689 passengers in 2025. It takes 93 per cent of all passenger traffic into Puerto Rico and 90 per cent of the air cargo.

The location is unusually good. The airport sits in the beachfront resort district of Isla Verde, four to seven miles from the Condado resort area, the Hato Rey financial district and Old San Juan, so transfers are short whichever of those a client is heading for.

The terminal naming needs care. The airport has switched between letters and numbers over the years and now uses both: letters for the concourses and numbers for the airline departure areas in Terminals B, C and D. Terminal A, opened in June 2012, is used solely by JetBlue and has its own ticketing area.

It is run by Aerostar Airport Holdings under a 40-year partnership that began in 2013, and as of 2025 it is the only privatised airport in the United States and its territories.

It is named after Luis Muñoz Marín, Puerto Rico's first popularly elected governor.
after:
Puerto Rico's main airport and the busiest in the insular Caribbean, handling more than 13.6 million passengers in 2025. It takes about 93 per cent of Puerto Rico's air passengers.

The location is unusually good: about seven miles east of central San Juan and a short drive from Puerto Rico's largest hotels, so transfers are short.

Terminals A to D are in use and Terminal E is closed. Terminal A, the newest, opened in June 2012.

Aerostar Airport Holdings runs it under a 40-year lease from the Puerto Rico Ports Authority that began in 2013. It is named after Luis Muñoz Marín, Puerto Rico's first popularly elected governor.

Worth restoring when the operator's site can be read.
